title: Asymmetric cavity seed with expanded Bragg mirrors (29-layer SiO2/Al2O3)
scientific_hypothesis: Breaking the central cavity symmetry (layers 11-13 initialized at 66.0/67.5/69.0 nm instead of uniform 67.5 nm) while adding 2 period pairs to each Bragg mirror will enable the optimizer to redistribute spectral gain into sharper transition slopes, improving the target score beyond the 0.379 plateau observed in prior route_03 iterations.
design_principle: 1-D photonic crystal filter with periodic main-function units sandwiched between anti-reflection coatings, following the SiO2/SiNx design methodology but adapted to SiO2/Al2O3 material pair for UV transparency.
proposed_topology: 29 finite coating layers: [SiO2/Al2O3]_7 Bragg mirror | asymmetric 3-layer cavity (SiO2/Al2O3/SiO2) | [Al2O3/SiO2]_7 Bragg mirror, total 29 layers on fused silica substrate
design_variables: optimization bounds ±20% around quarter-wave at 267.5 nm
manufacturing_considerations: ALD or IAD recommended for thickness uniformity
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for periodic stack optimization
Asymmetric cavity initialization breaks optimization symmetry lock-in
Expanded Bragg mirror periods widen stopband bandwidth
expected_advantages: Wider stopband from additional mirror periods
Escaped local minimum from asymmetric seed
Improved transition sharpness between passband and stopband
known_risks: Increased layer count may amplify thickness tolerance sensitivity
Asymmetric seed may converge to different local minimum not necessarily better
execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer SiO2/Al2O3 multilayer coating on fused silica substrate for solar-blind UV bandpass filtering. Layer sequence: alternating SiO2/Al2O3 starting with SiO2 (layer 1), total 29 finite layers. Initialize layers 1-10 as quarter-wave at 267.5 nm (SiO2 ~39 nm, Al2O3 ~67.5 nm), layers 11-13 as asymmetric cavity (66.0 nm SiO2, 67.5 nm Al2O3, 69.0 nm SiO2), layers 14-29 as alternating Al2O3/SiO2 quarter-wave. Optimization bounds: ±20% around initialization. Objective: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with coherent TMM solver. Air incidence, unpolarized or average of s/p. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Per feedback directive: break symmetry lock-in by seeding central cavity block (layers 11-13) with asymmetric profile (66.0/67.5/69.0 nm) instead of identical 67.5 nm; add 2 period pairs to Bragg mirrors (25→29 layers) to widen stopband and force optimizer to redistribute gain into sharper transition slopes.
